concepts.name: Embedded System
concepts.description: A computing system designed to perform a dedicated function inside a larger product, combining hardware and software while operating under constraints such as timing, memory, power, cost, and reliability.

concepts.name: Dedicated Function
concepts.description: A specific, single purpose that an embedded system is built to carry out within a larger product.

concepts.name: Hardware–Software Integration
concepts.description: The combination of hardware and software components that work together within an embedded system.

concepts.name: Resource Constraints
concepts.description: Limitations on timing, memory, power, cost, and reliability that govern the design and operation of embedded systems.

concepts.name: Real-Time System
concepts.description: A system that must respond to events within defined timing constraints.

concepts.name: Deadline
concepts.description: A timing constraint in a real-time system that must be met to avoid failure or degradation.

concepts.name: Hard Real-Time
concepts.description: A real-time system where missing a deadline can cause system failure.

concepts.name: Soft Real-Time
concepts.description: A real-time system that tolerates occasional deadline misses without catastrophic consequences.

concepts.name: Microcontroller
concepts.description: An integrated chip containing a processor core, memory, timers, and peripheral interfaces, optimized for controlling physical devices and interacting with sensors and actuators.

concepts.name: Processor Core
concepts.description: The central execution unit within a microcontroller that processes instructions.

concepts.name: Memory
concepts.description: On-chip storage within a microcontroller used to hold program code and data.

concepts.name: Peripheral
concepts.description: A device or interface connected to a controlling processor that provides specialized functions such as timing, communication, or data conversion.

concepts.name: CPU
concepts.description: The central processing unit that executes instructions in a computing system.

concepts.name: Program Memory
concepts.description: Memory that stores the program code executed by the CPU.

concepts.name: Data Memory
concepts.description: Memory that stores runtime data used by the CPU during program execution.

concepts.name: Peripheral Interface
concepts.description: An interface providing specialized functions such as timers, serial communication, analog conversion, and digital input/output.

concepts.name: GPIO
concepts.description: General-Purpose Input/Output pins that allow a microcontroller to read digital signals and control external devices.

concepts.name: Digital Input
concepts.description: A GPIO pin configuration that reads a digital signal from an external device such as a switch.

concepts.name: Digital Output
concepts.description: A GPIO pin configuration that drives an external device such as an LED.

concepts.name: Pin Configuration
concepts.description: The setup of a GPIO pin as either an input or an output to interact with external devices.

concepts.name: Floating Input
concepts.description: An unconfigured digital input that can produce unpredictable signal readings.

concepts.name: Pull-Up
concepts.description: A resistor configuration that establishes a default high logic level on a digital input line until an external device changes the state.

concepts.name: Pull-Down
concepts.description: A resistor configuration that establishes a default low logic level on a digital input line until an external device changes the state.

concepts.name: Logic Level
concepts.description: The default voltage state (high or low) established on a digital input line by a pull-up or pull-down resistor.

concepts.name: Sensor
concepts.description: A device that converts a physical quantity such as temperature, light, pressure, or motion into an electrical signal that a controller can measure.

concepts.name: Physical Quantity
concepts.description: A measurable property of the physical world, such as temperature, light, pressure, or motion, that sensors detect and convert.

concepts.name: Electrical Signal
concepts.description: The voltage or current representation produced by a sensor that corresponds to a measured physical quantity.

concepts.name: Measurement
concepts.description: The process of determining the value of a physical quantity through sensor and signal conversion.

concepts.name: ADC
concepts.description: An Analog-to-Digital Converter that maps a continuous electrical signal to a discrete numerical representation.

concepts.name: Analog Signal
concepts.description: A continuous electrical signal that represents a physical quantity and requires conversion for digital processing.

concepts.name: Digital Representation
concepts.description: A discrete numerical value produced by an ADC to represent a sampled analog input.

concepts.name: Resolution
concepts.description: The granularity of an ADC's output, determining how finely the input range can be represented as a discrete value.

concepts.name: Interrupt
concepts.description: A mechanism that temporarily transfers processor control to an interrupt service routine when an event requires immediate attention, resuming normal execution afterward.

concepts.name: Interrupt Service Routine
concepts.description: The routine executed by the processor in response to an interrupt, which handles the event and then returns control to the normal program flow.

concepts.name: Event
concepts.description: An occurrence detected by hardware or software that may require immediate processor attention.

concepts.name: Processor Context
concepts.description: The current state of the processor that must be saved and restored during an interrupt transition.

concepts.name: Polling
concepts.description: A method of repeatedly checking whether an event has occurred, as opposed to being notified by hardware.

concepts.name: Interrupt-Driven Design
concepts.description: A design approach where hardware notifies the processor when an event occurs, improving responsiveness compared to polling.

concepts.name: Responsiveness
concepts.description: The ability of a system to react promptly to events, improved by interrupt-driven design over polling.

concepts.name: Event Handling
concepts.description: The overall mechanism for detecting and responding to events through polling or interrupt-driven approaches.

concepts.name: UART
concepts.description: An asynchronous serial communication protocol using transmit and receive lines, with data framed by start and stop bits at a configured baud rate.

concepts.name: Serial Communication
concepts.description: Data transfer between devices one bit at a time over a single communication line, as used by UART.

concepts.name: Baud Rate
concepts.description: The configured speed at which UART serial data is transferred, measured in bits per second.

concepts.name: Data Frame
concepts.description: The structure of a UART transmission, including start and stop bits framing the data.

concepts.name: I2C
concepts.description: A synchronous serial bus using clock and data lines that supports multiple addressed devices communicating with a controller.

concepts.name: Synchronous Bus
concepts.description: A communication bus that uses a shared clock signal to coordinate data transfer between devices, as in I2C.

concepts.name: Addressing
concepts.description: The method by which individual devices on a shared bus are identified and selectively communicated with.

concepts.name: Controller
concepts.description: The device on a bus (e.g., I2C master) that initiates and manages communication with addressed peripheral devices.

concepts.name: RTOS
concepts.description: A real-time operating system that provides scheduling and synchronization mechanisms for applications with multiple concurrent activities and timing requirements.

concepts.name: Scheduling
concepts.description: The process by which an RTOS determines which task executes, often based on priority and timing requirements.

concepts.name: Concurrency
concepts.description: The condition where multiple tasks or activities execute or overlap in time, requiring coordination when accessing shared resources.

concepts.name: Timing Requirement
concepts.description: A constraint defining when an action must be completed, motivating the need for a real-time operating system.

concepts.name: Task
concepts.description: A discrete unit of application behavior managed by an RTOS scheduler, which decides execution order based on priority and timing.

concepts.name: Scheduler
concepts.description: The RTOS component that determines which task executes at any given time, typically based on priority and timing constraints.

concepts.name: Priority
concepts.description: A value assigned to a task that influences the scheduler's decision of which task to execute first.

concepts.name: Context Switch
concepts.description: The process of saving the state of one task and restoring the state of another to transfer processor execution between tasks.

concepts.name: Shared Resource
concepts.description: A data or hardware resource accessed by multiple concurrent tasks, requiring coordination to avoid inconsistent results.

concepts.name: Race Condition
concepts.description: An inconsistency that arises when concurrent operations on a shared resource interleave without proper coordination.

concepts.name: Mutex
concepts.description: A synchronization mechanism providing controlled exclusive access to a shared resource.

concepts.name: Semaphore
concepts.description: A synchronization primitive that can coordinate events or control access to a limited number of shared resources.

concepts.name: Mutual Exclusion
concepts.description: The principle of ensuring only one task accesses a shared resource at a time, enforced by mechanisms such as mutexes.

concepts.name: Synchronization
concepts.description: Coordination of concurrent tasks or events using mechanisms such as mutexes and semaphores.

concepts.name: IoT
concepts.description: A system architecture that connects physical devices to networks and software services, spanning sensing, local processing, communication, data storage, and application layers.

concepts.name: Edge Device
concepts.description: A physical device at the edge of an IoT system that performs sensing and local processing before communicating with network services.

concepts.name: Network
concepts.description: A communication infrastructure connecting IoT edge devices to cloud services and software platforms.

concepts.name: Cloud Service
concepts.description: A remote software platform in an IoT architecture that receives, processes, and stores data transmitted from edge devices.

concepts.name: Data Pipeline
concepts.description: The end-to-end flow of data through an IoT system from sensing through local processing, communication, storage, and application layers.

concepts.name: Telemetry
concepts.description: The collection and transmission of measurements from an embedded device, involving validation, timestamping, transmission, and storage of data.

concepts.name: Timestamp
concepts.description: A time marker attached to a measurement to record when it was taken, used in telemetry pipelines.

concepts.name: Data Validation
concepts.description: The process of verifying that sensor readings are correct and reliable before further processing in a telemetry pipeline.

concepts.name: Data Transmission
concepts.description: The transfer of measured data from an embedded device to a storage or processing destination over a communication interface.

concepts.name: Storage
concepts.description: The retention of collected and transmitted measurements for later analysis in a telemetry pipeline.

concepts.name: Temperature Monitoring
concepts.description: An embedded application that reads a sensor through an ADC, periodically samples the value using a scheduled task, transmits measurements via a communication interface, and stores telemetry for analysis.

concepts.name: Sampling
concepts.description: The periodic acquisition of sensor values at regular intervals using a scheduled task for monitoring purposes.

concepts.name: Scheduled Task
concepts.description: A task in an RTOS that executes at regular intervals to perform periodic operations such as sensor sampling.

concepts.name: System Integration
concepts.description: The process of combining requirements, hardware interfaces, software tasks, timing behavior, and data flow into a complete embedded solution, verifying each dependency before integration.

concepts.name: Requirements
concepts.description: The specifications and dependencies that must be verified before integrating an embedded system.

concepts.name: Hardware Interface
concepts.description: The physical and electrical interfaces (e.g., GPIO, ADC, UART, I2C) that connect an embedded system's components.

concepts.name: Software Task
concepts.description: A discrete unit of software behavior in a complete embedded solution that must be verified in the context of system integration.

concepts.name: Data Flow
concepts.description: The movement of data through an embedded system from sensing and input through processing to output and storage.
